title: The Sunken Vault of Kelimor
summary: Descend into a flooded dwarven vault beneath a mountain lake to reclaim a stolen relic — before something ancient reclaims you.
world: The Ironspire Mountains loom over the northern reaches of the kingdom of Valdris, their peaks perpetually capped with cloud. Lake Kelimor sits high in these peaks — a cold, black body of water that has no visible inlet and no visible outlet. Below the lake lies the ruins of Kelimor Deepstone, a dwarven hold abandoned three centuries ago when a catastrophic underground flood burst through its foundations and drowned three-quarters of its population overnight. The survivors never returned. Now the vault lies half-submerged: its upper halls reachable by rope and rusted iron ladder, its lower chambers sealed beneath dark, motionless water. The dwarven clans of the lowland settlements consider the site sacred ground and curse those who plunder it. Treasure hunters consider it cursed and plunder it anyway. Both groups have a point. The vault is laid out across three tiers: the Entry Halls (dry, crumbling stone, collapsed chambers), the Flooded Crossing (a great central corridor flooded knee-to-waist deep with black water), and the Deep Vaults (fully submerged, accessible only by diving or via drained side-passages). Creatures encountered here include undead dwarven clockwork constructs still executing their final patrol orders, giant blind cave fish that hunt by vibration, and a drowned revenant — the spirit of Kelimor's last Vault-Warden — that guards the Counting Hall on the second tier. The climate inside is cold enough to see breath. Everything echoes.
openingScene: You arrive at the lake's edge as the sun sinks behind the peaks. A rusted iron door, propped open by some past expedition that didn't bother closing it behind them, stands flush with the cliff face at the water line. Beyond it, worn stone steps descend into shadow, their lower reaches swallowed by dark, motionless water. Your lantern catches a flicker of gold somewhere below — could be ore in the rock, could be something else. The half-dwarf merchant named Tolven who hired you said the Relic of Calling is in the Counting Hall on the second tier, and that it 'shouldn't be guarded by anything serious.' He said this while not making eye contact. The scratching sounds coming from below the waterline are new. Tolven did not mention those.
rulesNotes: Standard D&D 5e. Underwater mechanics: holding breath uses Constitution modifier + minutes formula; swimming costs double movement unless the character has a swim speed. Torches last 1 hour, lanterns (with oil) last 6 hours — the DM tracks usage and narrates when light is running low. Darkness in the vault beyond torchlight is total; darkvision functions normally. Environmental hazards include loose stone (Dexterity saving throws when running), freezing water (Constitution saving throws after extended immersion, DC 10 per minute, failure = exhaustion level), and unstable ceilings (the DM may call for checks or describe collapses). The drowned revenant (treat as Revenant stat block, CR 13) is only encountered if the player reaches the Counting Hall — it will not pursue beyond the second tier. Dwarven clockwork constructs (use Animated Armor stat block, CR 1) patrol in pairs. Combat should feel dangerous and tactical; fleeing and retreating are valid strategies. Recommended character level: 3–5. Tone: tense, atmospheric, claustrophobic. Reward clever thinking over brute force.
